subject: general
question: A can do a certain work at the same time in which B and C together can do it. If A and B together can do it in 7 days and C alone in 9 days, then B alone can do it in ______ days.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total efficiency of **A + B + C** = (1/7) + (1/9) = 16/63 units per day.

Given **Efficiency of A = Efficiency of (B + C)**.

∴ Efficiency of **A** = (1/2) × (16/63) = 8/63.

Efficiency of **B** = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of A = (1/7) − (8/63) = (9 − 8)/63 = 1/63.

**∴ The correct answer is 63 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by (A + B) = 7 days, Time taken by C = 9 days.

⇒ Combined Efficiency of **A + B + C** = 9 + 7 = 16 units/day.

⇒ Since **A = B + C**, then **A + (B + C) = A + A = 2A**.

⇒ 2 × Efficiency of **A** = 16 ⇒ Efficiency of **A** = 8 units/day.

⇒ Efficiency of **B** = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of A = 9 − 8 = 1 unit/day.

⇒ Time taken by **B alone** = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of B = 63 ÷ 1 = 63 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 63 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Efficiency Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. **Total Work = Efficiency × Time**.

LCM Method

To find **Total Work**, take the **LCM** of the individual days taken by the workers to complete the work.

Combined Work Formula

If two people work together with efficiencies **E₁** and **E₂**, their combined time **T = Total Work ÷ (E₁ + E₂)**.</p
